Title: Malaysia to repatriate first batch of 1,476 Myanmar nationals on Sept 29
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 27 — The Home Ministry (KDN) has finalised the first phase of a voluntary repatriation programme that will send 5,000 eligible Myanmar refugees back to their home country in stages, the ministry announced in a statement today.
The first batch of the Voluntary Repatriation Programme will proceed on September 29, involving 1,476 Myanmar nationals identified by Myanmar's government through a diplomatic note dated August 13.
The date was agreed at a coordination meeting involving the Home Ministry, Foreign Ministry, National Security Council and Defence Ministry, after accounting for logistical needs — moved back from Myanmar's original proposal of August 28. The operation will use two Myanmar naval warships and a hospital ship.
The move follows Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan's remarks on August 14, when he said Malaysia would prioritise the safety and welfare of Myanmar refugees ahead of any return, stressing that verification with the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) and KDN was essential to assess the security situation returnees would face.
He had also said Malaysia did not need to wait until all 5,000 were ready, and that an initial group of 1,000 already verified could be sent back first. He added that Asean regarded the Myanmar refugee crisis as a serious, collective concern that should continue to be addressed through the bloc's Five-Point Consensus.
According to today's KDN statement, of the Myanmar nationals slated for processing this year, 4,008 — mostly ethnic Rohingya — will be channelled into the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme, while the remaining 5,000 will undergo the phased voluntary repatriation.
The ministry said that as of August 15, there were 10,388 Myanmar nationals held at Immigration Detention Depots, cautioning that this figure covers all detained Myanmar nationals and should not be read as entirely refugees. The Immigration Department, working with police, is verifying each individual's identity, citizenship, immigration status, asylum claims and security background, with the DPP registration exercise for this group expected to conclude in the fourth quarter of 2026.
KDN described its approach as "two-pronged": continuing diplomatic negotiations with Myanmar to ensure an orderly, staged and accountable return of its nationals, while simultaneously registering and profiling individuals claiming refugee or asylum status through the DPP programme to give the government comprehensive data for monitoring, enforcement and eventual resolution — including repatriation when conditions allow.
The ministry said the DPP scheme will eventually be expanded to cover all undocumented migrants outside detention depots, including UNHCR cardholders, with registration made mandatory to obtain biometric and personal data. Those who qualify will receive a DPP card allowing temporary stay under conditions set by the government.
KDN noted that more than 95 percent of refugees in Malaysia are from Myanmar, including Rohingya, Chin, Karen and Mon communities, and reiterated that a resolution cannot be unilateral, requiring continued direct diplomatic engagement with Naypyidaw.
The statement stressed that Malaysia is not a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol, and that the DPP programme should not be construed as recognition of or accession to those instruments. Instead, it described the DPP as reflecting the government's own humanitarian approach, balanced against national interest and sovereignty, aimed at addressing what it called a decades-long unresolved issue that has become a financial burden and a security concern.

Title: Nepal embassy in KL appeals for flood relief donations as death toll rises
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Nepal government has accorded high priority to search, rescue, relief and emergency response operations in areas affected by the devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi River on Wednesday, according to the Embassy of Nepal in Kuala Lumpur.
The embassy said the flood had caused significant loss of life and extensive damage to property and infrastructure, particularly in the Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Gorkha districts.
“The relevant authorities and security agencies are continuing their efforts to locate and rescue those affected, provide immediate assistance and assess the full extent of human casualties and physical damage,” the embassy said in a statement posted on Facebook on Thursday.
Meanwhile, it said the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers had appealed to individuals, organisations, businesses and well-wishers to extend financial assistance to support the safe relocation of affected people and their long-term rehabilitation and recovery.
In this regard, the embassy has appealed to Nepali nationals residing in Malaysia, Nepali associations and organisations, businesspersons, social workers and well-wishers of Nepal to provide financial support for those affected by the devastating flood.
Financial support can be channelled into the official bank accounts of the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund and the Prime Minister’s Relief Fund at Rastriya Banijya Bank (account numbers: 1130100003762001/ 1130100000006006) and Nepal Bank Limited (account numbers: 00211600510039000003/ 00200100510039000001).
The full list of bank accounts and their QR codes is available in the embassy’s Facebook post. — Bernama

Title: From outdoors to indoors: Haze forces National Day Eve switch as PM’s address moves from Dataran Merdeka to PICC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The National Day 2026 Prime Minister’s Address scheduled for August 30 will be moved from Dataran Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur to the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) due to the current haze, the Communications Ministry said today.
The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 9.30pm, according to a media statement issued by the National Day and Malaysia Day Celebration Working Committee.
“The decision was made as an adjustment in view of the current situation, particularly to ensure the safety, health and comfort of guests and the public, as well as to ensure the smooth implementation of the ceremony,” the statement said.
“The relocation of the venue does not affect the content or spirit of the National Day 2026 celebrations, but is instead a responsible measure to ensure the ceremony can be held in a more controlled and comfortable environment.
“The government will continue to monitor the haze situation and air quality developments from time to time,” it added.
The decision comes as haze has continued to affect several parts of the country this past week, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading over 100 in over a dozen areas.
Sarawak and the Greater Klang Valley – which also includes Putrajaya – have been recording some of the worst readings, at times crossing 200.
Good API air quality is set at 0–50, moderate at 51–100, unhealthy at 101–200, very unhealthy at 201–300 and hazardous at above 300.
The government had on Wednesday said it was reviewing the scale and location of this year’s National Day celebrations because of the deteriorating air quality, although cancellation was not being considered.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the review covered both the Aug 30 National Day eve programme at Dataran Merdeka and the main Aug 31 celebration in Putrajaya, with health and safety the key considerations.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also expressed hope that the haze would ease in time for the National Day and Malaysia Day celebrations.
“We pray to Almighty God that the haze remains under control so that the celebrations can take place,” he said on Wednesday.
The committee said a decision on the National Day parade scheduled for August 31 would be made based on the prevailing conditions and advice from the Health Ministry, Department of Environment and Malaysian Meteorological Department.
The public has also been advised to remain alert to the latest haze situation and obtain health information and advice through the Health Ministry’s official channels.
The Malaysian and Indonesian governments also agreed earlier this week to step up preventive measures against transboundary haze, with authorities warning that the El Niño phenomenon was expected to intensify towards October.

Title: Nepal floods: Tok Mat says Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu searching for 55 missing citizens
Article:
JEDDAH, Aug 27 —  Fifty-five Malaysians are reportedly still unaccounted for following major flooding in Nepal, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said, although the figure has yet to be confirmed by Nepalese authorities.
He said the information, provided by travel agencies, is being gathered and cross-checked by the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu.
“We have tried to contact them but have received no response. They have therefore been placed on the list of those still missing, while Nepalese security agencies are carrying out search and rescue (SAR) operations,” he said in an interview with Bernama here on Thursday.
Mohamad is leading Malaysia’s delegation to the extraordinary meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), in Doha.
Mohamad said the effort to locate them is proving difficult due to damaged access routes and disrupted roads and bridges.
According to him, the latest information from the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu and Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs indicated that authorities are conducting SAR operations for those still missing.
“We have received reports describing the flooding as a massive inland tsunami, which caused many deaths and left many people still missing,” he said.
Mohamad said Malaysia had deployed additional personnel from Dhaka, Bangladesh, to Kathmandu to assist the Malaysian Embassy in handling the situation by monitoring the operation, managing the welfare of Malaysians, and coordinating with Nepalese security authorities.
“We sent additional personnel from Dhaka because it is roughly a one-hour flight to Kathmandu,” he said.
Regarding the possibility of Malaysia deploying rescue teams and other forms of assistance, Mohamad said the National Security Council would decide the matter.
He also conveyed his sympathies and condolences to the families of Malaysians who have yet to be located.
“My condolences and deepest sympathies go to the families of all Malaysians who remain missing or unaccounted for,” he said, adding that he prayed they would be found. — Bernama

Title: MIC’s Saravanan says he is the ex-minister being charged tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan has confirmed that he will be charged in the Sessions Court here tomorrow.
The Tapah MP claimed that he will face charges stemming from a third-party statement linking him to the issue of hiring foreign workers during the Covid-19 pandemic in 2022.
Saravanan, who is also the MIC deputy president, claimed that the initial statement linking his name was made by an individual who just died two months ago, before the individual involved later made a statutory declaration (SD) to withdraw the allegations.
“I stress that I have never contacted or known the individual either via phone or short messaging service. Even though the main witness has died, I am still prepared to defend myself and face this charge according to the law,” he said in a video message shared with the media today.
Saravanan said tomorrow, his legal team will apply to the court for the trial of the case to be expedited without any delay.
Today, a media invitation was issued by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) regarding a former minister to be charged at the Sessions Court here tomorrow.
The former minister is expected to face charges under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009 relating to the act of soliciting, receiving, giving, promising or offering a bribe. — Bernama

Title: Zara Qairina inquest: Handwriting on loose sheets matches mysterious ‘Wina’
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 27 — Several loose sheets examined in connection with the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir showed similarities with handwriting attributed to a declared writer identified as “Wina”, the Coroner’s Court heard today.
Forensic document examiner Tay Eue Kam said the handwriting on loose sheets marked Y9B, Y10A and Y10B showed similarities with handwriting attributed to the declared writer Wina in an indented impression recovered from page 50i of the olive-green “Love And Peace” journal marked WK9.
She said this during the questioning by lawyer Joan Goh, counsel for one of the teenagers charged in the bullying case involving Zara Qairina.
Tay said the indented impression on WK9 page 50i was recovered using the Electrostatic Detection Apparatus (ESDA), and agreed that it could have originated from a missing or torn page or another page that had previously been placed above page 50.
However, Tay told the court that she did not have an actual specimen handwriting of ‘Wina’ for comparison.
“I do not have the specimen (actual) writing of Wina per se, but what I had was the writing declared as Wina on page 50i of WK9,” she told Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan during the inquest into Zara Qairina’s death here today.
When Goh asked whether they knew if Wina existed, Tay replied: “I don’t know.”
Tay further testified that Y9B, Y10A and Y10B were grouped together following comparisons involving entries from Y1A to Y15B.
Her report stated that differences were observed between the handwritten entries in the group and Zara Qairina’s specimen handwriting, providing strong support that Zara Qairina did not write those entries.
Asked specifically whether Y9B, Y10A and Y10B were written by Wina, Tay maintained that the handwriting characteristics were similar to those attributed to the declared writer Wina.
On the contents of Y9B, which touched on matters concerning Zara Qairina’s mother, Tay said she was not in a position to explain the content.
During further questioning, Tay confirmed that her report did not contain a specific comparison chart for Y9B, Y10A and Y10B, although she maintained that similarities and differences had been analysed.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious in a drain near her school hostel at about 4 am.
The inquest is scheduled to continue from Sept 7 to 11, with Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist Dr Chua Sze Hung and Chemistry Department Document Examination Division officer Nurul Atiqah Mohd Noh expected to be recalled.
This will be followed by testimony from Zara Qairina’s father and stepsister, while the locus in quo inspection has been fixed for Oct 5. — Bernama

Title: 1MDB ex-CEO says he took Jho Low’s word on Petrosaudi deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) chief executive officer Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi told the High Court today that he believed fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho or Jho Low’s information about the proposed US$2.5 billion joint venture (JV) signing ceremony between the company and PetroSaudi International Ltd (PSI) as there had been early communication with the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), in 2009.
The 56-year-old, who is testifying as the fourth plaintiff witness in the US$5.64 billion suit filed by 1MDB and its four subsidiaries, said that, if he recalled correctly, there had been initial communication with former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s then special officer Datuk Amhari Efendi Nazaruddin during the early preparations for the proposed ceremony.
He said the communication gave him reason to believe that the proposed ceremony would take place. However, Shahrol Azral acknowledged that he did not pursue the matter further and had no documentation confirming that the ceremony was to take place.
He said this during cross-examination by Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, who represents Najib, the first defendant in the suit.
Muhammad Shafee: Amhari is one other interesting witness, less colourful than you, but still colourful. You agree, Amhari, one of those confirmed receiving money from Jho Low?
Shahrol Azral: I don’t have knowledge on that.
Muhammad Shafee: All this information about the signing ceremony came from Jho Low?
Shahrol Azral: Yes.
Muhammad Shafee: And you took it as true?
Shahrol Azral: Yes.
Previously, in the 1MDB’s criminal trial involving Najib, the court was told that the signing ceremony never happened, despite it being the reason the deal was hastily done in the first place.
1MDB and its subsidiaries – 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited, 1MDB Energy Limited, 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited and Global Diversified Investment Company Limited, formerly known as 1MDB Global Investments Limited – filed the civil suit on May 7, 2021.
They named Najib, 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng, former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee, former general counsel Jasmine Loo Ai Swan, Vincent Beng, former chief financial officer Radhi Mohamad, former 1MDB investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jin, and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.
Recently, 1MDB dropped its civil suit against Radhi, with no liberty to refile. The company had previously removed Jasmine from the case as well.
The writ of summons stated that the plaintiffs, among other things, accused the defendants of breach of trust, breach of statutory duty, abuse of power and conspiracy to misappropriate 1MDB funds.
The trial before Judicial Commissioner (JC) Mohamad Redzuan Idrus continues on March 15 next year. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin trial: Witness admits testifying to avoid corruption charges, but denies getting MACC ‘immunity’ deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A key prosecution witness today agreed that he had come to court to testify against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, in order to save himself from being charged in his own corruption case.
Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, 54, president of the Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) and managing director of Bumiputera-owned KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, confirmed this as the prosecution’s 27th witness.
When asked by High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin to clarify if his motive in coming to court as a prosecution witness was to save himself from corruption charges against him, Azman replied “agreed”.
Just before Noor Ruwena’s question, Azman however said he was unsure when asked the same question by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik.
Earlier today, Azman confirmed that he was a suspect in the MACC’s previous investigations on Jana Wibawa.
Azman’s case is based on a January 2023 complaint to the MACC alleging that he and other individuals had solicited and received bribes from contractors as a reward to help them obtain RM4.9 billion worth of Jana Wibawa projects.
Azman confirmed that his company KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and his relative’s company Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd had received a total of RM9.35 million from several constructors including RM1 million from Nepturis Sdn Bhd and RM600,000 from Mamfor Sdn Bhd.
But he disagreed with Hisyam’s suggestion that this meant that there was basis to the 2023 complaint to the MACC on the allegations that he had asked for and received bribes in connection with Jana Wibawa projects.
Azman also disagreed that Nepturis Sdn Bhd’s appointment letter to appoint KCJ Engineering as a consultant for a RM1 million payment was a “sham” to hide his receiving of bribes, and disagreed that he had made a “complete lie” in court when saying that KCJ Engineering did provide consulting services to Nepturis.
Among other things, Azman disagreed that the companies KCJ Engineering and Addeen Engineering would get more money as a reward, if he got more companies to participate in getting projects under Jana Wibawa.
Azman denied misusing or selling Muhyiddin’s name in order to convince these contractors.
Azman agreed he had an interest in Addeen Engineering which he said belonged to his in-law, and later confirmed that his son is a director in Addeen Engineering.
Azman confirmed that the MACC investigation against him has not been given a “No Further Action” (NFA) status, and that meant that the case against him was still live.
Just before this confirmation, he disagreed with Hisyam’s suggestion that he was testifying as an MACC witness against Muhyiddin to avoid being prosecuted for corruption charges.
When Hisyam suggested he could be charged for seeking and accepting bribes as there was evidence to show this, Azman said he was unsure.
Earlier, Azman said it was not odd that he had not been charged for receiving RM1 million from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, while Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad was charged for receiving RM2 million from the same company for helping it to obtain a Jana Wibawa project.
Hisyam: Not odd because you and MACC have made an understanding, a deal where you come to court, give evidence against Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, you will be given immunity, agree or not?
Azman: Disagree.
Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex on August 27, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
This afternoon, Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad repeatedly sought to cast doubt on the accuracy of Azman’s testimony, by challenging the contractor on whether he had actually met with Muhyiddin in July 2020 at the Tropicana Golf Club.
Yesterday, Azman said that Muhyiddin had in the July 2020 meeting told him that the government had approved the Jana Wibawa programme, and that the then prime minister had “spontaneously” said contractors could donate directly to his party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.
At one point, Amer pointed out that the Cabinet had only approved the Jana Wibawa programme in November 2020.
Amer suggested that this meant Azman’s claim about Muhyiddin’s Jana Wibawa programme remark was a “figment of your imagination as a result of watching and reading fiction books and stories”, but the businessman disagreed.
Azman yesterday said he and KCJ Engineering had donated RM4.8 million to Bersatu after securing a RM62 million government project under Jana Wibawa, while Nepturis had also been shown in this trial to have given RM1 million to Bersatu after getting a RM141 million project under Jana Wibawa.
Shahradzi Shamsuddin had previously also testified that his company Mamfor donated RM19.5 million to Bersatu as his younger brother’s company Sutracom Sdn Bhd was awarded a RM605.2 million project under Jana Wibawa.
Azman yesterday said all these donations were due to Muhyiddin’s spontaneous remark that contractors could donate directly to Bersatu instead of to individuals in Bersatu.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial is scheduled to resume on September 1.

Title: Lubok Antu only Sarawak area with very unhealthy API reading as of 4pm
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 27 — Lubok Antu was the only area in Sarawak to record a “very unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) reading this afternoon, as haze continued to affect several parts of the state.
According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) Sarawak’s Daily Haze Watch, Lubok Antu recorded an API reading of 210 as of 4pm today, placing it in the very unhealthy category.
Four other areas — Samarahan, Sri Aman, Lundu and the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD Serian) monitoring station — recorded unhealthy air quality, with readings ranging from 156 to 158.
Samarahan recorded the highest API reading among the four at 158, followed by Sri Aman at 157, while Lundu and IPD Serian each recorded 156.
The readings indicate that haze conditions remained particularly pronounced in parts of southern and eastern Sarawak, while air quality in Kuching and most other divisions remained at moderate levels.
Kuching recorded an API reading of 88 at 4pm, placing it in the moderate category.
Other areas with moderate readings were Sarikei (85), Bintulu (86), Samalaju (83), ILP Miri (77), Mukah and Miri (72 each), Sibu (70), Lawas (66), Kapit (65), Bario (60), Limbang (58) and Tebedu (95).
NREB classifies API readings of 101 to 200 as unhealthy, while readings between 201 and 300 are considered very unhealthy.
According to the board, very unhealthy air quality can aggravate existing health conditions and reduce tolerance for physical exercise among people with heart and lung complications, while also posing a wider risk to public health. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak minister: Dialogue key to resolving issues with Indonesia (VIDEO)
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 27 — Sarawak will continue to resolve issues with neighbouring Indonesia through dialogue and engagement rather than allow matters such as the haze to escalate into conflict, said Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
He said the approach was consistent with the spirit of the Malaysia-Indonesia Peace Agreement 1966, which ended the Indonesian Confrontation through dialogue, diplomacy and the willingness of both sides to seek common ground.
“The most important lesson of 1966 is how the conflict ended — through dialogue, through diplomacy, through sincerity, and through the willingness of neighbouring nations to seek common ground,” he said his speech at the 60th anniversary of the Malaysia-Indonesia Peace Agreement 1966 commemorating the end of the Indonesia-Malaysia confrontation at Batu Lintang Memorial Square here today.
He said the same spirit remained relevant in managing present-day issues between Sarawak and its Indonesian neighbours, including the recurring haze situation.
“In many other countries, problems like this might lead to war. But down here, we try to resolve our problems amicably behind the scenes,” he said.
Abdul Karim said Sarawak had been engaging the Indonesian government over fires in West Kalimantan which had contributed to the haze affecting the state.
“We have been behind the scenes, we have been trying to tell them — especially the Indonesian government — please control those fires because this has become an annual occurrence,” he said.
He stressed that peaceful management of differences was important given the close historical, cultural and people-to-people ties between communities on both sides of the Borneo border.
“Our borders may define our countries, but they do not erase the connections between our people. Instead, they provide an opportunity for us to build bridges of cooperation,” he said.
Abdul Karim said Malaysia and Indonesia had transformed their relationship over the past six decades from confrontation to cooperation and mutual respect, working together in trade, tourism, education, culture, security and people-to-people relations.
He said Sarawak’s close ties with Kalimantan were reflected in practical cooperation, including energy and humanitarian assistance.
“Sarawak is now exporting electricity to West Kalimantan,” he said, adding that Sarawak Energy was also helping supply electricity to Indonesia’s new capital, Nusantara.
He also recalled Sarawak’s assistance to West Kalimantan during the Covid-19 pandemic, when the state supplied oxygen to hospitals there amid shortages.
Abdul Karim said the Aug 11, 1966 peace agreement represented a decision by Malaysia and Indonesia to turn a new page and look towards the future.
“The future can always be different from the past,” he said.
He also paid tribute to Malaysian, Australian, New Zealand, British and Gurkha servicemen who served in Borneo during the Confrontation, including those who made the ultimate sacrifice.
“Their presence here reminds us that the history of Borneo is also part of a wider history of regional cooperation and friendship,” he said.
Abdul Karim said the presence of veterans at the memorial was a powerful reminder of how far Malaysia-Indonesia relations had progressed.
“Yesterday, we served during difficult times. Today, we stand together in friendship. And tomorrow, we move forward together in peace,” he said.
He said the lesson of the 1966 agreement should be passed to younger generations by emphasising reconciliation and the peaceful resolution of differences.
“Peace is not simply the absence of conflict. Peace is the result of understanding. Peace is built through dialogue. Peace is strengthened through cooperation. And peace is sustained through friendship,” he said.
Abdul Karim called on Malaysia and Indonesia to continue strengthening their ties and for Borneo to become a region where borders are bridges, where communities prosper together, and where friendship prevails over division. — The Borneo Post

Title: Police find no evidence stress contributed to Hulu Selangor teacher’s death
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 27 — The investigation into the death of a female teacher at a school in Hulu Selangor has so far found no evidence linking stress to the victim’s death.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said a detailed investigation, including statements recorded from various parties, such as family members, colleagues and students, found that the victim had been in good condition before the incident.
“Statements have been recorded from family members, colleagues and students, but they did not point to or confirm any element of stress, as alleged, as she appeared to be doing well.
“However, the case is still being investigated as a sudden death report (SDR), and police are working to gather further statements before referring the investigation papers to the Deputy Public Prosecutor, together with recommendations for further action,” he said at a press conference at the Selangor contingent police headquarters (IPK), here, today.
He said the female teacher had been serving as a teacher for several years, but had only recently transferred to and served at the school for less than a year.
In addition, police have yet to find any leads or personal problems linked to the victim’s death.
On July 30, a female teacher was found unconscious at a school in Hulu Selangor district, before she was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at Kuala Kubu Bharu Hospital. — Bernama

Title: Shah Alam brawl that killed man linked to secret society turf war, says Selangor police chief
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 27 — Police believe a brawl that resulted in the death of a man at Taman Alam Megah here two days ago was caused by a feud and turf war between two secret society groups.
Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said that initial investigations revealed that both groups operate in and around the state capital and are involved in several business activities.
“Initial investigations show that the incident is linked to a hostility or turf war between two secret society groups, one of which is believed to have been recently established in this district.
“To date, we have detained 11 individuals aged between 20 and 39, comprising members from both groups. Five have been remanded for seven days, while the remaining six were brought to court today for remand applications,” he told a press conference at the Selangor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) here today.
He said police are investigating the business activities and backgrounds of the groups involved in the clash. They are also searching for several suspects who remain at large after being identified during initial investigations.
Shazeli said the incident at Jalan Mandolin 33/5 also injured several people, including three victims still receiving hospital treatment.
“Statements from eyewitnesses at the scene and relevant parties have been recorded to assist in completing the investigation paper. Detailed investigations are underway under the provisions of the law to identify the leaders and the leadership structure of the secret societies involved,” he said.
A one-minute video dated August 23 circulated online, showing a group of people fighting on the road and one person being struck by a vehicle.
Meanwhile, on the attempted robbery at a jewellery shop in Klang on August 20, Shazeli said the incident involved no loss of jewellery or injuries, but police have obtained positive leads.
“The police are conducting a detailed investigation to identify suspects involved in the attempted robbery. Thanks to information and assistance from the public, we have obtained several positive leads.
“The suspects are believed to be locals who planned the crime by lying in wait for an opportune time to strike,” he said.
Shazeli said investigations are continuing based on closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and other physical evidence to track down all the suspects. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry: No new gambling licences issued under Madani govt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Finance Ministry today described recent remarks by Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor on gambling licences in the state as misleading, saying the Madani government has not issued new gambling licences or increased the number of gambling premises.
The ministry said Sanusi’s remarks, recently reported by the media, could give the impression that the Madani government was not controlling gambling activities or had approved new licences to increase the number of gambling premises in Kedah.
“Throughout the federal government’s administration from 2020 to 2022, which also included PAS, there was never any proposal or decision to ban licensed gambling activities nationwide or abolish existing licences,” it said in a statement.
The ministry said records showed that the Pakatan Harapan federal government in 2020 had decided to reduce the number of special draws from 22 to eight a year.
“Subsequently, the federal government under Perikatan Nasional and Barisan Nasional in 2020 decided to increase or restore the frequency of special draws to 22 times a year,” it said.
“After the Madani government took over the federal administration in late 2022, one of its first decisions was to reverse the increase and reduce the frequency of special draws from 22 to eight times a year, effective January 2023,” it added.
The ministry stressed that the Madani government had never issued any new gambling licences or permits and had not increased the number of new gambling shops.
“The number of licences and permits in force remains based on the number of existing licence approvals since the 1990s,” it said.
“As a control measure, the Finance Ministry has also imposed strict conditions on licence holders,” it added.
The ministry said the Madani government continued to adopt a firm and responsible approach by limiting licensed gambling activities, ensuring strict regulation and stepping up enforcement against unlicensed and online gambling.

Title: Cabinet gives in-principle nod to Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan elevated expressway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Cabinet has given in-principle approval for the proposed development of the Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan Elevated Expressway (BSE), Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said today.
He said the decision reflected the Madani government’s commitment to providing high-impact infrastructure that benefits the public, stimulates economic growth and sustainably enhances the country’s competitiveness, according to a report by national news agency Bernama.
Nanta said BSE, a proposed strategic infrastructure project, could strengthen the transport network and connectivity in Greater Kuala Lumpur by serving as a high-capacity link integrating several major expressways.
“These include the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, Maju Expressway (MEX), Besraya Expressway (BESRAYA), New Pantai Expressway (NPE), Shah Alam Expressway (KESAS) and the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Dispersal System (SPRINT) network.
“The development of an elevated expressway along this strategic alignment has the potential to provide an alternative route for road users and facilitate movement between the northern, southern and east coast corridors of Peninsular Malaysia,” he said in a statement today.
Nanta said improved connectivity would enhance public mobility, strengthen logistics efficiency and facilitate the movement of goods, while potentially reducing travel times and improving access to employment centres, educational institutions and public services.
He said, in line with the Malaysia Madani aspiration, BSE was not merely the construction of a new expressway but a long-term investment in strengthening connectivity, inclusive development and the country’s economic competitiveness.
“Following the in-principle approval, the Works Ministry, together with relevant agencies including the Public Private Partnership Unit (UKAS), will continue negotiations and detailed assessments to finalise the project’s implementation structure.
“The government will ensure every aspect of the project is comprehensively assessed, particularly in terms of public interest, value for money for the country and fiscal sustainability, before any final decision on its implementation is made,” he said.
Nanta said the proposed BSE development would also be guided by a private-sector financing approach, ensuring its implementation would not involve direct financial commitments from the federal government.
He said the government would also selectively examine other infrastructure solutions to complement the road network and address traffic congestion in the Klang Valley.
The proposals would be considered based on strategic needs, capacity improvements and their impact on traffic flow.
“KKR will continue to ensure that the subsequent process is carried out carefully, transparently and based on the interests of the people and country, in line with the government’s commitment to developing a more efficient, integrated and sustainable transport system to support economic growth and improve the quality of life of the people,” he said.

Title: Ismail Sabri out on RM300,000 bail after son settles payment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob left the court complex here today after his son paid the RM300,000 bail imposed on him.
The 66-year-old Bera MP declined to comment on the charges against him, instead leaving the matter to his legal team led by Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad,
Berita Harian
reported.
Asked about his health, Ismail Sabri replied: “Yes.”
He then shook hands and greeted supporters who had travelled from Bera to show their support.
The supporters waited outside the court complex lobby for more than two hours.
Also seen were former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin and former Pahang menteri besar Tan Sri Adnan Yaakob.
Ismail Sabri was then escorted by supporters as he made his way to his vehicle.
A supporter who wished to be known as Rohaina said she was relieved to see Ismail Sabri in good health after the former prime minister experienced health problems several weeks ago.
“I am relieved to see that he has recovered but sad that he has to face charges in court. I hope he will be acquitted of the charges,” she said.
Declare assets under Section 36(2) of MACC Act
Earlier, Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin allowed Ismail Sabri to be released on RM300,000 bail with one surety after he pleaded not guilty to a charge of failing to comply with a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) notice.
The notice required him to declare his assets under Section 36(2) of the MACC Act 2009.
However, Suzana rejected the prosecution's application for Ismail Sabri to surrender his passport as there was no evidence to suggest he was likely to flee the country.
Ismail Sabri arrived at the court complex at about 8.35am with his wife Datin Seri Muhaini Zainal Abidin and children, including singer Dafi, before being joined by supporters and other family members.
He appeared calm in the public gallery as he chatted with his siblings and supporters.
Khairy, Adnan and former Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun were also present for the proceedings.
The public gallery was filled with journalists and security personnel, while only individuals with valid court passes were allowed entry.
Ismail Sabri, dressed in a black suit, entered the dock at 9.38am before Suzana ordered the charge to be read to him.
He appeared calm as he indicated that he understood the charge and elected to stand trial.
The charge was also displayed on a television screen in the courtroom, where Ismail Sabri read and examined the details, including the foreign currencies allegedly involved.
After the proceedings, supporters approached Ismail Sabri to offer words of encouragement before he was taken to a temporary holding room next to the courtroom.
Meanwhile, his son, accompanied by lawyer Datuk Seri Rajan Navaratnam, went to the bail payment counter to settle the amount.
Pacemaker fitted
Meanwhile, Amer Hamzah said his client was recovering well after undergoing a pacemaker implantation procedure at the National Heart Institute (IJN) and was scheduled for a follow-up examination.
“I am relieved that nothing bad happened today. Let us continue to pray for his health,” he said.
Asked about Ismail Sabri’s feelings over the charges against him, Amer Hamzah said: “No one likes being charged, especially when you believe the charges are baseless and have strong grounds.”

Title: Two Fire and Rescue dept officers among Malaysians uncontactable after Nepal flash floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Two Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) officers are among the Malaysians who remain uncontactable following flash floods in Rasuwa, Nepal.
JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said they are its Planning and Research Division deputy director Mohd Sani Harul and Central Region Academy officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa.
He said the two officers were part of a group of 10 Malaysians who left for Nepal on Monday night and were travelling to Everest Base Camp (EBC).
“One is a senior fire officer and the other is a fire officer. They were on their way to EBC. They were not climbing, but travelling by jeep along the Tibet route,” he told Bernama when contacted today.
He added that Mohd Fakhrul Munir was among those who took part in the ‘Bomba de Everest Mencari Hati Emas’ charity climbing expedition to Mount Everest in 2025.
Wisma Putra said in a statement today that families have been unable to contact more than 50 Malaysian travellers in Nepal following Wednesday’s devastating floods in which hundreds of foreigners and Nepalese remain unaccounted for. — Bernama

Title: MACC gets seven-day remand for former Tabung Haji chairman, ex-Treasury sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A politician who previously served as Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and a former Treasury secretary-general have been remanded for seven days to assist in ongoing graft investigations into the pilgrimage fund.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) also obtained a four-day remand extension for a former TH chief executive officer who had already completed an initial seven-day detention period.
The three suspects arrived at the Putrajaya Court Complex at 9.30am under heavy guard for the remand proceedings,
Kosmo
reported.
Both the former TH chairman and the former finance ministry secretary-general, who are in their 60s, were arrested at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya at around 4pm on Wednesday.
MACC chief commissioner Abd Halim Aman confirmed yesterday that the case is being probed under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009 for using one’s office or position to solicit gratification.
The arrests are part of the MACC crackdown following the declassification of the royal commission of inquiry (RCI) report on TH’s management, operations and assets from 2014 to 2020.

Title: Penang leaves fate of agency chairman under corruption probe to Putrajaya
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 27 — The Penang government will defer to Putrajaya on the status of a federal agency chairman currently under investigation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) for alleged abuse of power in a land disposal deal.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow also said that the state respects the MACC’s jurisdiction and will allow the agency to conduct its probe without interference.
“I believe this is under the MACC’s jurisdiction and we are giving the MACC space to continue its investigation,” Chow said when asked for comment.
Addressing whether the chairman should be suspended, Chow clarified that the authority lies with the federal government, as the entity in question is a federal agency rather than a state-run body.
“It is up to the federal government as it is a federal agency, not a state agency,” he added.
The case emerged last Friday when the MACC remanded five individuals to assist in investigations into the disposal of land owned by a federal agency in Penang.
The suspects included the agency's chairman, two company directors, a technical manager, and a female clerk.
The chairman, a Datuk in his 50s, is suspected of abusing his former roles as deputy chairman and board member in 2015 to sanction the sale of eight plots of land in South Seberang Perai.
The land was allegedly sold to a company linked to his associate at below-market prices, resulting in estimated losses of approximately RM1.96 million.
The MACC is continuing its investigation into the matter while the chairman was released on RM10,000 bail yesterday following the completion of a week-long remand.

Title: Safe and sound: Malaysian hikers at Annapurna Base Camp unaffected by Nepal-Tibet floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A group of Malaysian hikers at the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trekking area has been reported safe following a flash flood at the Nepal-Tibet border believed to have been caused by a glacier collapse yesterday.
Freelance tour guide Muhammad Hafizal Hamidon said the Malaysian hikers in the area were not affected as the location of the flash flood was far from their trekking route.
“Alhamdulillah, so far everyone here is safe and well. Although it rained quite heavily yesterday afternoon, we are safe here and there are also many other Malaysians in this area.
“The incident occurred in the Langtang Valley, which is quite far from our trekking route to ABC,” he told Bernama Radio when contacted today.
Muhammad Hafizal and his group, who are now on the fourth day of their trek to ABC, said none of their fellow hikers or Malaysians had been identified as being affected by the tragedy.
Commenting on the current situation and the movement out of the trekking area, he said the road access route back to the city was understood to have been slightly disrupted following the incident.
“Based on information from the guides and trekking organisers, the route for us to leave may be slightly affected, but it is expected to be resolved within a few days.
“The road is expected to be restored before we complete our trek,” he said, confirming that his group is scheduled to return home on Aug 31.
Meanwhile, he advised Malaysians in Nepal to always follow the instructions of local guides and keep their whereabouts updated to avoid causing concern among family members back home.
Muhammad Hafizal also advised those planning to undertake trekking activities in Nepal in the near future to postpone their plans temporarily due to unpredictable weather conditions and the high risks involved.
A total of 55 Malaysians reported to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu are currently uncontactable following floods and destruction caused by the overflowing Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa District, Nepal, on Aug 26, according to the Foreign Ministry.
In a statement today, the ministry said this was based on the latest information received from family members, travel agencies and other relevant sources. — Bernama

Title: Sunway Lagoon roller coaster accident that landed two in hospital now under Selangor police probe for possible negligence, sabotage
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 27 — Police are conducting a detailed investigation into an accident involving a roller coaster ride at the Sunway Lagoon Theme Park last Saturday to determine whether there were elements of negligence or sabotage.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the investigation was being conducted in collaboration with several other agencies, including the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department and the Selangor Department of Occupational Safety and Health, focusing on technical expertise.
“We have held discussions with the agencies concerned and, ultimately, we will cross-check the findings to determine the actual cause of the accident,” he said at a press conference at the Selangor contingent police headquarters here today.
He said two victims were still receiving treatment at a hospital, but neither had sustained serious injuries, while the other affected victims had been discharged or were receiving outpatient treatment.
Elaborating on the follow-up action at the site, Shazeli said the ride had been temporarily suspended pending completion of the probe, allowing the team to conduct a detailed inspection of its physical structure and control room.
Meanwhile, he said police had also recorded statements from several witnesses, including theme park operations staff, ride attendants and the victims involved, to assist in the investigation.
“A thorough investigation is ongoing to complete the relevant information, and police are not disregarding any new leads that emerge throughout the investigation process,” he said.
Last Monday, Subang Jaya police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat was reported to have said that 10 individuals sustained minor injuries in a roller coaster incident at a theme park.
The incident occurred at about 9 pm on Saturday, while a police report was lodged at 11.45 am on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Dengue cases jump 60.8pc as MOH weighs vaccine rollout due to high cost
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 27 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is still conducting comprehensive studies and evaluations before making the dengue vaccine part of the National Immunisation Programme (NIP), said its minister, Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
Dzulkefly said that the studies also included a cost-benefit analysis, considering that the price of the newly marketed dengue vaccine is still quite high.
“I know that one vaccine has obtained approval and has been registered by the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) and is being used in private facilities. Do give us some time...we are currently conducting a cost-benefit analysis on a dengue vaccine from Japan.
“To make it part of the NIP is not easy. We have to study it carefully ... besides that, there are several other vaccines in the planning by the Health Ministry. We are waiting for reasonable ones and will announce them if we make a decision,” he said to reporters.
Dzulkefly said this after officiating the Negeri Sembilan Dental Specialist Centre (PPPNS), an event also attended by the Health deputy director-general (Oral Health) Dr. Zuraida Mohamed, who is also the State Health director Dr. Zuraida Mohamed, here today.
He said over 61,000 dengue cases have been reported nationwide up to Epidemiological Week 33 of 2026 (until Aug 22), an increase of 60.8 per cent compared to the same period last year, with 58 deaths recorded.
Therefore, he said, the MOH activated the dengue operations room and deployed personnel to areas identified as hotspots, especially in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, as well as expanding the use of the Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes as a biological control method.
Dzulkefly said that efforts to combat dengue are not only the responsibility of the MOH, but also require the cooperation of all parties, including local authorities and related agencies, to ensure that residential areas and premises do not become breeding grounds for the Aedes mosquitoes.
Meanwhile, he said the health ministry is reviewing the proposal to expand its basic dental screening and treatment into the PeKa B40 scheme and will implement it as soon as possible after receiving approval.
He said that dental programmes should be given attention as part of preventive treatment and primary healthcare, particularly in the management of non-communicable diseases (NCD).
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said the PPPNS, with a cost of RM32 million, is the first dental specialist referral facility outside a hospital environment in Malaysia, and since operating from Sept 25, 2025, it has handled 11,085 patients as of this June.
According to him, the PPPNS functions as a central zone reference hub covering Negeri Sembilan, Selangor, the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, and Melaka, benefitting 11.89 million residents.
“With the addition of 18 modern dental chairs, our daily treatment capacity has surged by nearly 90 per cent from 80 patients to 150 patients per day, and the waiting period for specialist treatment has also decreased from two months to two to three weeks,” he said.
He also said the transformation is driven by the Dental Information System, in addition to modern imaging facilities and skill labs that serve as centres for continuous clinical training to hone the competencies of dental staff.
“This centralised model will be expanded to other states in phases, starting with zonal levels such as the central zone in Negeri Sembilan and the Borneo zone before continuing by state to ensure equitable access to services,” he added.
The MOH is also continuing to improve public access to basic dental services through outreach programmes, with eight new Mobile Dental Clinics set to be received by the end of this year in Sabah, Perlis, Penang, Selangor, Putrajaya and Johor. — Bernama

Title: King voices concern over Malaysians caught in Nepal floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has urged Wisma Putra to take all necessary measures to assist Malaysians affected by the floods in Rasuwa, Nepal.
According to a post on the Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar Facebook page today, His Majesty directed that the latest information on their safety and whereabouts be provided to their respective family members.
“I have been following developments surrounding this tragedy since it was reported yesterday.
“I also urge Wisma Putra to take all necessary measures, including providing their family members with the latest information on the safety and whereabouts of the Malaysians involved,” he said.
His Majesty also prayed that all efforts to rescue and evacuate the affected Malaysians would proceed smoothly.
According to the post, Sultan Ibrahim and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, expressed their concern and prayed for the safety of the Malaysians affected by the disaster.
“Their Majesties pray for the safety of all the victims and that they will be granted ease in dealing with the situation,” it said.
Wisma Putra said in a statement today that families have been unable to contact more than 50 Malaysian travellers in Nepal following Wednesday’s devastating floods in which hundreds of foreigners and Nepalese remain unaccounted for. — Bernama

Title: After ex-PM Ismail Sabri, MACC says ex-minister to be charged with corruption tomorrow
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 27 — A former federal minister is set to be charged in the Sessions Court tomorrow in connection with a corruption-related offence, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) announced today.
In a media invitation, the anti-graft agency confirmed it has obtained the necessary approval to proceed with the charges, although the identity of the former minister has not been disclosed.
The accused is expected to be produced before the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court at 9am.
It is understood that the former minister will be charged under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009, which pertains to the solicitation, receipt, promising, or offering of gratification.
Earlier today, former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was charged today with failing to declare his assets under Section 36(2) of the MACC Act, becoming the third Malaysian ex-PM to be criminally charged.

Title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 17 Malaysians on Mount Kailash pilgrimage out of contact, another group led by Everest climber N. Mohanadas safe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Seventeen Malaysians travelling to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China, for a pilgrimage have been unreachable for more than 24 hours following devastating flash floods near the Nepal-Tibet border yesterday, raising concerns among their families.
R. Logadashini said four of her family members – her father S. Raman, 59; mother M. Neelavany, 54; uncle S. Murukan, 60; and aunt G. Padmahwathi, 58 – were among the 17 Malaysians in the group organised by Nepal-based Fishtail Tours & Travels.
She said the group arrived in Nepal on Aug 23 and was scheduled to continue its pilgrimage until Sept 5.
“The last direct communication with the tour group was recorded at about 8.18 am Nepal time yesterday (10.33 am Malaysian time), when they were reported to be about two kilometres from the Nepal-Tibet Immigration Checkpoint.
“After that, all contact with the group was lost. We tried contacting the agency and the Malaysian Embassy but, as of now, we have not received any information,” she said when contacted by Bernama.
She said her family’s last WhatsApp message was received at about 8.40 am Malaysian time yesterday.
Meanwhile, Wisma Putra said 55 Malaysians reported to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu were currently uncontactable following the floods, but it has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties so far.
The Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu is working closely with the Nepalese authorities, search and rescue teams, travel agencies and other relevant parties to establish the safety and whereabouts of the Malaysians.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered relevant government agencies to urgently locate and contact Malaysians affected by the floods, with Malaysian diplomatic missions in Kathmandu and New Delhi having been mobilised to assist.
Flash floods struck areas in Nepal’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts after heavy rain and a glacial collapse, disrupting communications and cutting off key roads linking the affected area with the capital, Kathmandu, hampering rescue efforts and access to those affected.
The route is commonly used by pilgrims travelling to Mount Kailash and trekkers heading towards the Everest region.
Meanwhile, another group of Malaysian pilgrims led by legendary Malaysian Everest climber Datuk N. Mohanadas has been confirmed safe in Tibet.
Mohanadas said his group of 56 people, including 39 Malaysians, four Singaporeans and three Canadians, was unaffected by the floods and was continuing its pilgrimage safely.
“We were aware of the sudden downpour, flash floods and casualties at the Nepal-Tibet border. Thankfully, our group and our route have not been affected, and we are continuing our journey safely.
“We have started our first of three days of pilgrimage to Mount Kailash to perform the auspicious Kailash kora (circumambulation) trek,” he said. — Bernama

Title: National Day in Putrajaya: 80,000 visitors, nearly 4,000 police, plenty of road closures but 103 shuttle buses to get you there
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A total of 3,811 Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) officers and personnel are fully prepared to ensure security and smooth traffic flow ahead of the 69th National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya.
Putrajaya police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said of the total, 2,357 officers and personnel had been deployed for static security and traffic control.
“A total of 1,755 officers and personnel have been assigned for static security, comprising personnel from the Kuala Lumpur contingent police headquarters (IPK), Selangor IPK, Putrajaya district police headquarters (IPD), as well as reinforcements from Bukit Aman to manage the influx of visitors, which is expected to reach 80,000,” he told Bernama when met today.
The detailed planning for the National Day celebration also involves cooperation from various agencies, including the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF), Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), Civil Defence Force (APM), People’s Volunteer Corps (Rela) and Putrajaya Corporation.
On the traffic management plan, Aidi Sham said road closures and diversions would be implemented in stages according to two main phases to minimise disruption to the flow of public traffic.
He said the first phase began yesterday, involving the full closure of Persiaran Perdana and Dataran Putra until Aug 29, from 6 am to noon, while traffic control will be implemented at Jalan Laman Perdana, Jalan P2A, Jalan P2T, Jalan P2S, Jalan P2W and Jalan P2Y.
“The second phase will begin as early as 5 am on Aug 30 until 6 pm on Aug 31, involving the closure of all major access routes to the Core Island Putrajaya area,” he said.
Aidi Sham said the main routes and bridges involved in the full closure during the second phase are Seri Wawasan Bridge, Seri Saujana Bridge, Seri Gemilang Bridge, Putra Bridge and Seri Ehsan Bridge.
He said the roads involved in the full closure during the second phase are Lebuh Bestari, Lebuh Setia, Lebuh Saujana, Lebuh Gemilang, Lebuh Wawasan, Lebuh Sentosa, Jalan Tun Hussein, Persiaran Barat and Persiaran Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah (PSSAAS).
He added that residents around Core Island P18 will be able to use Seri Bestari Bridge and Seri Setia Bridge.
He advised the public to plan their journeys, arrive early at the celebration venue and use public transport to avoid traffic congestion.
“A total of 103 free shuttle buses have been provided by Putrajaya Corporation to ferry visitors to and from two main pick-up points, namely Putrajaya Sentral and the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC), directly to Dataran Putra.”
Meanwhile, Aidi Sham also stressed that the airspace throughout Putrajaya had been gazetted as a no-fly zone for drones from the rehearsal sessions until the day of the celebration, and the public is strictly prohibited from operating any drones without permission from the authorities.
Visitors are also reminded not to bring sharp or dangerous items to ensure that the event environment remains safe, smooth and peaceful for everyone to enjoy with their families. — Bernama

Title: Follow the rules when recruiting abroad, tourism minister tells MM2H agents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing has urged MM2H Programme agents to comply with the laws of the countries where they operate when promoting the programme and recruiting participants overseas to prevent confusion and fraud.
He said having a licence to operate in Malaysia did not automatically mean MM2H agents had fulfilled the regulatory requirements of other countries.
“Agents who have obtained MM2H licences in Malaysia should not assume that they have fulfilled all regulatory requirements. When promoting MM2H and recruiting clients in other countries, they must also understand local laws and cooperate with local authorities,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Tiong said the matter was among the issues discussed during a meeting with the Malaysian Association in the Republic of Korea during his recent visit to the country, which was also attended by its president Dr Aaron Kim Hong-Seok, secretary-general Kim Jun-Hyung and several other representatives.
According to him, the association representatives told him that some MM2H agents in Malaysia might not fully understand the regulatory system and were dealing directly with local individuals, resulting in many parties claiming that they could handle MM2H applications.
Tiong said he would remind all MM2H agent companies to comply with all applicable rules and regulations upon his return to Malaysia.
“We cannot simply look at the number of applicants brought in. What matters most is protecting applicants and ensuring that the market develops in a transparent, legal and orderly manner,” he said.
He said a clearer cooperation mechanism between MM2H agents in Malaysia and local industry partners in key markets was important to reduce ambiguity, prevent fraud and misunderstandings, and enhance confidence in the programme among prospective foreign applicants.
Tiong said the Korean market had strong potential for MM2H, especially among retirees looking to make Malaysia their second home during the winter months.
He hoped MM2H agents would continue to intensify promotional efforts in the Korean market and collaborate with local industry partners to ensure more effective promotion of the programme. — Bernama

Title: Penang keeps close eye on haze situation before final decision on Merdeka parade
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 27 — The Penang state government is closely monitoring daily air quality levels before making a final decision on the upcoming Merdeka parade at the Esplanade.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow noted that because the National Day celebrations on Aug 31 are held outdoors, any significant deterioration in haze conditions could jeopardise the event.
“The minister said yesterday that if the situation worsens, the event could be conducted indoors,” Chow said during a press conference at his Komtar office today.
However, he admitted that relocating the parade is practically unfeasible.
“Even if we move it to the stadium, it is still out in the open,” he added.
The state will rely on the air pollutant index (API) to determine the viability of the parade. Chow said that if readings hit 200 API or above, the government would likely cancel the proceedings.
“But it is still a few days away. We will monitor it closely,” he said, adding that no definitive decision has been made yet.
The urgency comes as API readings in Penang have fluctuated between moderate and unhealthy levels (50 to 160) over the past few days.
Parallel to the event planning, Penang youth, sports and health committee chairman Daniel Gooi confirmed that the state health department is on high alert for any spike in respiratory-related illnesses.
“But so far, in the state of Penang, everything is still under control,” Gooi said.
He noted that there has been no sudden surge in such cases, but said all public healthcare facilities have still been placed on standby.
“We encourage the public, should you suffer any respiratory-related symptoms, feel free to attend any of our healthcare facilities to seek treatment,” he said.

Title: Foul smell leads to discovery of body in aircraft wheel compartment at KLIA2
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — An unidentified body was found inside the wheel compartment of an aircraft at Kuala Lumpur International Airport 2 (KLIA2) today.
The body, whose gender has yet to be determined, was discovered at about 6.55am inside the wheel compartment of an aircraft from Tokyo, Japan, which landed at about 6.30am, according to a
Berita Harian
report.
The body, believed to be wearing jeans and a white shirt, was found by engineering staff assigned to open the aircraft’s wheel compartment.
Based on information received, the staff detected a suspicious foul smell coming from the compartment before opening it and discovering the body, after which they informed the KLIA2 police station operations room.
The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Forensics Unit was subsequently called to the scene to conduct further investigations.
Preliminary investigations found that the victim was believed to be in their 20s and had likely been dead for more than 72 hours.
However, no identification documents were found on the body.
Further investigations are underway to establish the victim’s identity and cause of death.

Title: CAAM officer killed after RXZ crashes under car in Tawau
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) Tawau air traffic officer died after the Yamaha RXZ he was riding is believed to have skidded and ended up underneath a Toyota Camry at Batu 3, Jalan Apas, in Tawau, Sabah, yesterday.
The 55-year-old local man sustained head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene after the 6pm incident,
Berita Harian
reported.
Tawau district police chief Assistant Commissioner Rosdi Mat Jusoh said preliminary investigations found that both vehicles were travelling in the same direction when the incident occurred.
He said the 28-year-old local man driving the Toyota Camry was travelling from Kampung Titingan towards Batu Payung, while the victim was riding his motorcycle from Tawau town towards Taman Millenium.
“When the Toyota Camry continued moving after the traffic lights at the Batu Hijau junction, the victim’s motorcycle was on the right side of the car and is believed to have lost its balance.
“This was due to the uneven road surface,” he said in a statement today.
Rosdi said an initial inspection at the scene found that the right lane had recently been resurfaced and was at a higher level than the left lane, which had yet to be resurfaced.
“The condition is believed to have caused the victim to lose his balance before falling in front of the Toyota Camry.
“The car driver was unable to brake in time, causing the victim and his motorcycle to become lodged underneath the front of the vehicle,” he said.
The Toyota Camry driver was unhurt, while the victim’s body was taken to Tawau Hospital for a post-mortem.

Title: Marine police officer shot while colleague unloads firearm in Lahad Datu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A Marine Police Force (PPM) officer was injured after being shot while on duty at the Marine Guard Post in Lahad Datu, Sabah, yesterday.
The Lance Corporal sustained injuries to the middle finger of his left hand and abdomen, according to
Harian Metro
.
Lahad Datu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Dzulbaharin Ismail said police received a report on the incident on the same day.
He said the officer was shot while a colleague was unloading a firearm at the scene.
“The victim received initial treatment at Lahad Datu Hospital before being referred to Tawau Hospital for further treatment.
“His condition was reported to be stable and he remains under treatment and observation at the hospital,” he said in a statement today.
Dzulbaharin said the case was being investigated under Section 37 of the Arms Act 1960 concerning the offence of discharging a firearm and causing injury to another person.
“Investigations are ongoing to determine the actual circumstances of the incident,” he said.
